title: Studio object designer: an edit made less than 1.5 s before switching to another object in the rail is silently discarded (the autosave debounce never sends it and no confirm is shown)
body:
domain:devx#1 · sunhaolin · session_017xRBcUoS2G4jgqRskpExS7

Found in the 18.3.0 release-candidate browser walkthrough (wave anchor #27377, card W3-UX), at framework `main` @ `c4c515ad`, Console built in-repo from the same commit.

## Repro (fresh boot)

1. Boot `examples/app-showcase` with `--seed-admin` and sign in as admin. Viewport 1440×900.
2. From Home choose **New in Studio**, create a package (e.g. "Field Service"), and create an object **Work Order** with an optional Number field **Estimated Hours** and a Picklist **Status** (option value `new`, label `New Request`). Create a second object, **Site**.
3. On Work Order's **Form** tab, add a Text field **Temp**. Wait 3 s, until "Saved" shows.
4. Click **Remove "Temp"**. Within one second, click **Site** in the object rail, then click **Work Order** again.

The walkthrough measured this with a 150 ms and an 800 ms gap. A label rename followed by a switch 1 s later behaves the same.

## Expected

The removal is saved, or the switch asks first. The edit is complete and saveable, so it is not one the pillar is still holding.

## Actual

**Temp** is back, and it is still there after a reload. A renamed label likewise reverts to its old text. Nothing between the edit and the debounce firing shows that an edit is pending: "Saving…" or "Saved" appears only once it sends.

## Reading

`useDraftAutoSave` (`ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/studio-design/useDraftAutoSave.ts`) sends after a 1500 ms timer. The timer deliberately does not send once the open item has changed ("a switch since the edit left it with its item"), and `flush` exists for callers. The rail's object switch neither flushes nor confirms.

Related, closed: #26705 and #26845, for edits the pillar is still holding because they are not yet saveable. This case is a saveable edit caught inside the debounce window.
